stem_bark.text: The bark of Helicteres isora is greyish-coloured, rough and warty.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Helicteres isora is greyish-coloured, rough and warty.

seed.text: The seeds of Helicteres isora are 2-3 mm long and 1.5-2 mm wide and dark brown-coloured. There are numerous seeds in each follicle.

fruit.text: The fruit of Helicteres isora is a spirally twisted follicle . It is 4-6 cm long and 1-1.5 cm wide and beaked with a 4 cm peduncle.

flower.text:
The flowers of Helicteres isora are grouped in axillary and few-flowered cymes. The peduncle is 7 mm long. The calyx-tube is campanulate, irregularly lobed and 1.5 cm long and 5-8 mm across. The calyx is light yellow-coloured and finely pubescent. The corolla is composed of 5 red-coloured, glabrous, irregular and clawed petals. The gynandrophore is 3.5-4 cm long.
The androecium is composed of 10 stamens at the end of the gynandrophore. The style is filiform, curved and about 4 mm long with a simple stigma . The ovary is ovoid and 5-celled with numerous ovules in each cell. The buds are covered with short and white hairs. The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Helicteres isora grow alternately on the stem. The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is chartaceous and pubescent on both sides. The leaves have a 0.8-1 cm long petiole with a pair of ensiform stipules at the axil of the stalk. The leaf of Helicteres isora is 8-12 cm long and 6-8 cm wide. The shape of the blade is obovate, the apex is acuminate, the base is cordate and the margins are serrate. The venation of the leaf is digitate.

habit.text: Helicteres isora is a small-sized, thornless, multi-stemmed and deciduous tree .

reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :
    Helicteres isora is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).
  • Mode of pollination :
    Helicteres isora is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.
  • Seed dispersal :
    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits of Helicteres isora burst and scatter the seeds.

phenology.text: ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )
phenology.text_html:
• Flowering season : From July to December.
  • Fruiting season : From November to March
  • Seeding season : From November to March
  • Leaves falling : During the hot season.

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

veterinary.text: The leaves and tender parts of Helicteres isora are useful as fodder . Source : Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan

handicrafts.text: The fibre extracted from the inner bark of Helicteres isora is used for making container bags, rough sacking, sewing gunny bags and cattle harness. It is used to make cordage. Helicteres isora is used for the manufacture of paper. Source : Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan

reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :
    Helicteres isora is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas.
    Helicteres isora requires a sunny position in a well-drained soil.
  • Seed treatments :
    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
